### [llm-chat-completions-server 0.1a0](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/30/llm-chat-completions-server/#atom-everything)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-07-30

The llm-chat-completions-server 0.1a0 plugin enables LLM models to serve OpenAI Chat Completion style requests, leveraging content-addressable logs for conversation state de-duplication.

- The plugin supports OpenAI Chat Completion style requests, where each incoming message extends the previous conversation.
- It utilizes content-addressable logs from LLM 0.32rc1 to de-duplicate conversation messages using hashes of individual parts.
- The server runs on a specified port (e.g., 9001) and exposes all installed LLM models via a ChatGPT Completions compatible endpoint.
- Installation involves `uv tool install llm --pre`, `llm install llm-chat-completions-server`, and `llm chat-completions-server -p 9001`.

**Why it matters:** This allows LLM models to integrate seamlessly with systems expecting the OpenAI Chat Completions API, simplifying development and deployment.

### [llm 0.32rc1](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/30/llm-rc1/#atom-everything)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-07-30

LLM 0.32rc1 introduces a new schema for prompt/response details, utilizing content-addressable hash IDs for message de-duplication and supporting forked conversations, alongside new model support.

- New schema design improves capture of prompt and response details for current model families.
- Content-addressable hash IDs are implemented for stored messages, enabling database de-duplication.
- The update allows LLM to represent trees of messages for forked conversations.
- Support for gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, and gpt-5.6-luna models has been added.
- A significant schema change involves new tables; existing data is unaffected, but a logs.db backup is recommended.

**Why it matters:** This release enhances LLM's ability to manage and track complex conversational data structures and integrates with newer language models.

`llm` `schema` `database` `gpt`
